subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable batching/aggregation of outbound Telegram notifications

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in outbound Telegram notification digest policy, and should it live in the Telegram plugin, shared outbound delivery, or a plugin/hook extension surface?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but the fix chooses config shape, delivery timing, urgent bypass, media/thread semantics, persistence, and core-versus-plugin ownership.

options.title: Define durable digest policy
options.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush semantics before implementation.

options.title: Expose plugin hook only
options.body: Keep core lean by adding or documenting only the extension seam needed for an external digest plugin.

options.title: Keep immediate delivery
options.body: Treat throttling, streaming coalescing, and error cooldowns as the supported anti-spam mechanisms and narrow or close the request later.

recommendation.title: Define durable digest policy
recommendation.body: Choose the owner seam, config names, bypass rules, and SQLite-backed flush semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across shared channel delivery APIs, Telegram throttling, and product-boundary decisions.
